title: Run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog
goal: Add an engine-enforced per-run wall-clock limit (default 20700 s, overridable via template max_run_s or ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S) that kills the run's process group via zbuild_pg_kill, ends with timed_out disposition naming the in-flight stage and limit, and still runs release and persist.

steps.description: Write failing unit tests (TDD red) for limit resolution and watchdog clean exit. run-limit-precedence-test.sh asserts: template max_run_s beats ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S beats 20700; a non-integer or non-positive value in either source emits misconfigured and returns 1 (AC 5). run-watchdog-clean-exit-test.sh asserts: after a run that finishes within its limit, no process with _RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID remains (AC 6). Both tests must fail before any implementation — the functions they call do not yet exist.

Write failing integration tests (TDD red). run-timed-out-test.sh plants a stage that hangs (a plugin that sleeps indefinitely), sets a small max_run_s (e.g. 3 s), and asserts: run ends with timed_out disposition; the result names the in-flight stage and the limit; a child that ignores TERM is gone within TERM+10 s (spawn a subprocess that traps SIGTERM but does not exit — verify it is reaped); release and persist still run (ACs 1–4). Also asserts watchdog fires when the engine is stuck between stage dispatches, not only inside one (plant the hang in main() after one stage returns). resume-after-run-timeout-test.sh: run the same hang until timed_out, then resume; assert the resumed run is not stopped immediately (AC 7). Both tests must fail at merge-base.

Amend ADR-054 and ADR-025. ADR-054: add §9 defining max_run_s (template key), ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S (env override), engine default 20700 s, precedence order, and the validation rule (non-integer or non-positive is misconfigured for either source); add an '## Enforced by' section naming tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh and tests/integration/run-timed-out-test.sh. ADR-025: add timed_out to the abort-word list; add a paragraph describing the run-limit path (watchdog writes timed_out first, sends SIGTERM to runner PID, first-recorded-wins preserves timed_out over later sigterm write); extend the existing '## Enforced by' section. Remove ADR-054-stage-contract.md from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt so lint-adr-enforced-by now enforces the new section.

Add max_run_s support to the template loader. In load_template() in core/pipeline/template.sh, parse the top-level YAML key max_run_s into _TPL_MAX_RUN_S (validate it is a positive integer; if present but invalid, fail load_template with misconfigured). Add a template_max_run_s() accessor following the same pattern as template_stage_router_timeout (reads _TPL_SOURCE_FILE, returns empty string if the key is absent so the caller can detect no-override). This makes the template layer of AC 5 resolvable.

Add _runner_resolve_run_limit_s() to scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh, following the _route_resolve_knob pattern already in that file. Priority: call template_max_run_s() first; if non-empty validate it is a positive integer (misconfigured + return 1 if not); else check ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S (same validation); else use 20700. Write the resolved value to the global _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S. The unit test in step-1 exercises this function directly.

Register timed_out as a valid abort word in scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh. Add it to the word-list comment that gates _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel. No new function is needed: the existing first-recorded-wins logic means the watchdog writing timed_out before SIGTERM reaches the runner preserves the correct disposition over the sigterm write that the runner's signal trap would otherwise record.

Wire the watchdog and limit into core/pipeline/runner.sh. In main(): call _runner_resolve_run_limit_s; if it returns 1 exit misconfigured; otherwise arm the watchdog — a background subshell that sleeps $_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S, calls _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel timed_out, then sends SIGTERM to $$; store the PID in _RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID. In the EXIT trap: kill $_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID 2>/dev/null before dispatching always_run stages (this is the disarm path for AC 6). In _runner_end_on_abort: add a timed_out arm that maps to status aborted (resumable=true) and emits the run-end event with limit_s=$_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S and the current in-flight stage name. The process-group kill uses the existing zbuild_pg_kill with 10 s grace (TERM then KILL), satisfying AC 3. A resumed run gets a fresh limit because main() re-arms the watchdog on every invocation — no extra state needed for AC 7.

notes:
Prerequisite state: #1801 (stage-level limit) is listed as a prerequisite in the issue ('all three edit runner.sh main() and the exit trap') but is not yet present in the codebase (no ZBUILD_MAX_STAGE_S was found during exploration). The issue says this work reuses #1801's zbuild_pg_kill path — that function IS present in scripts/lib/proc-group.sh, so the TERM→KILL mechanism is available. The 10 s grace period is passed explicitly to zbuild_pg_kill rather than delegated to a non-existent #1801 constant. If #1801 lands before this, step 7 may need to align on how the grace constant is expressed.

Watchdog subprocess vs subshell: the watchdog is a background bash subshell (parentheses syntax). It will be in the runner's process group unless we use setsid or set -m. When the runner's SIGTERM trap fires zbuild_pg_kill on the run's process group, the watchdog (if still alive) will also receive TERM — this is harmless because by then the watchdog has already done its work (write sentinel + send SIGTERM to $$). The clean-exit test in step-1 checks that the watchdog PID is gone after a normal exit, which the EXIT trap's kill satisfies.

AC 8 (same behavior locally and in CI) is structural — no branch on platform, no read of GitHub's job limit. The integration tests run in CI, so CI coverage is automatic. No separate test is needed.

ADR enforcement baseline: config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt currently lists ADR-054-stage-contract.md, which exempts it from the Enforced-by lint. Step 3 removes that entry so the new §9 Enforced-by section is required by lint. ADR-025 already has an Enforced-by section (according to exploration notes) — step 3 extends it rather than creates it.

runner.sh line count: the file is already ~3975 lines, far above the 500-line guideline. Step 7 adds ~85 lines to it. This is justified because the issue requires editing runner.sh's main() and EXIT trap, and splitting the file is not in scope here. The resolver function is deliberately placed in stage-limits.sh (step 5) to minimize the runner.sh delta.

The integration test for AC 2 ('watchdog fires when engine stuck between stages') requires planting the hang at the engine loop level, not inside a stage dispatch. This means the test fixture needs a way to stall runner.sh's main() loop between stages — a stub plugin that returns success but then the engine delays before the next dispatch. The exact mechanism depends on runner.sh's inter-stage flow; if no external hook exists, the test may need to use a very short max_run_s and rely on the watchdog firing during a sleep the engine already does (e.g. a polling interval). This is a gap that the integration test author must resolve against the real runner.sh loop structure.

timed_out as a disposition word: ADR-054 §6a already defines timed_out as a valid disposition (from stage-level use). The run-level use in step 7 reuses it. The only new registration needed is in abort-propagation.sh's word-list comment (step 6) and the ADR-025 word list (step 3).
